newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HAYDEN LASHES FOURTH CHAMPIONSHIP CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HAYDEN LASHES FOURTH CHAMPIONSHIP CENTURY.

text.p: Australian Matthew Hayden smashed his fourth century in seven county championship innings for Hampshire on Wednesday.
The Queensland batsman extended his prolific sequence with a glorious 150 on the opening day of the four-day match against Northamptonshire at Northampton.
Hayden's innings, out of Hampshire's close of play score of 335 for four, lifted his first-class aggregate in his first season of county cricket to 899.
The Australian is on course to be the first batsman to reach 1,000 runs this northern summer.
Hayden reached three figures in 187 minutes off 155 balls, hitting 20 fours, and batted altogether for a shade under four and three quarter hours, finishing with 27 boundaries.
He shared a second wicket stand of 189 in 53 overs with Kevan James (56), then added 79 for the third wicket with exEngland batsman Robin Smith (71 not out).
Durham opener Jon Lewis frustrated leaders Kent with a face-saving innings of 129 not out on the opening day at Darlington.
He shared an unbroken stand of 88 with James Boiling (24 not out) as Durham recovered from 127 for seven to close on 215 for seven.
Zimbabwe leg-spinner Paul Strang helped to give Kent the early initiative with two wickets in two balls, but Lewis engineered a recovery in his 296-ball effort that contained 15 fours.

Surrey opener Jason Ratcliffe, seizing his chance while team mates Alec Stewart and Graham Thorpe are on England test duty, scored his first century for the county in a run spree against Worcestershire.
Ratcliffe hit 135, reaching three figures off 160 balls with 17 fours and a six off the first delivery of the day, as Surrey made 382 for seven by the close.
The former Warwickshire batsman and the aggressive Alistair Brown, who struck 121, dominated with a fourth wicket stand of 179 in 38 overs.
Ratcliffe made his 135 from 224 balls, hammering 22 fours and a six, while Brown completed his hundred from 107 balls. In all, he hit 18 fours and three sixes.
Iain Sutcliffe hit his maiden championship century as champions Leicestershire dominated the opening day against Somerset at Bath.
The former Oxford University batsman scored 112 in a total of 337 for three off 100 overs to complete a bad day for the home side.
They lost newly-capped pace bowler Andre van Troost with a hamstring injury and Pakistan leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed through a knee problem.
New captain Mark Ramprakash helped Middlesex recover from 47 for five to 237 all out against Gloucestershire at Bristol, where left-arm paceman Mike Smith took three for six in 21 balls.
Ramprakash's 75 and 79 from Keith Dutch lifted the visitors, before Gloucestershire slipped to 57 for three in reply at the close.
